subject: pathology
title: Pro-Inflammatory Cytokines: TNF, Interleukin-1, and Interleukin-6

steps.tx: Cytokines are low-molecular-weight regulatory proteins secreted by activated immune cells that mediate intercellular communication in host defense. In acute inflammation, the master orchestrators of local and systemic responses are three pro-inflammatory cytokines: **tumor necrosis factor, interleukin-one, and interleukin-6**, produced predominantly by antigen-stimulated macrophages and dendritic cells.
steps.say: TNF, IL-1, and IL-6 are master macrophage cytokines that coordinate local and systemic acute inflammation.

nodes.label: Microbial Endotoxins (LPS) Bind Toll-Like Receptor-4 on Macrophages
NF-Kappa-B Translocates into Nucleus, Driving Cytokine Gene Transcription
Secretion of Active TNF-Alpha, Interleukin-1-Beta, and Interleukin-6
Coordinates Endothelial Activation, Bone Marrow Mobilization, and Fever

steps.tx: Tumor necrosis factor is synthesized as a membrane-bound homotrimer that is cleaved by the metalloproteinase TACE into a soluble active cytokine. Released **tumor necrosis factor (TNF)** binds TNFR1 receptors on vascular endothelium to induce expression of E-selectin, ICAM-1, and VCAM-1, converting the resting lining into a pro-adhesive surface.
steps.say: TNF induces endothelial adhesion molecules like E-selectin and ICAM-1 to capture passing leukocytes.

left.title: Local Actions of TNF
points: Upregulates endothelial E-selectin, ICAM-1, and VCAM-1 adhesion molecules
Stimulates endothelial production of chemokines (CXCL8) and platelet-activating factor
Increases microvascular permeability by loosening intercellular tight junctions
Activates microbicidal respiratory burst and degranulation in neutrophils

right.title: Systemic Pathological Actions
points: Depresses myocardial contractility, lowering cardiac output in shock
Induces systemic vascular smooth muscle relaxation, causing severe hypotension
Promotes intravascular thrombosis by downregulating thrombomodulin
Causes chronic metabolic cachexia by suppressing appetite and lipoprotein lipase

steps.tx: Synthesized as an inactive thirty-one kilodalton precursor, interleukin-one beta requires proteolytic processing by the intracellular caspase-one inflammasome complex before secretion. Active **interleukin-one (IL-1)** shares biological actions with TNF, stimulating endothelial adhesion molecules, promoting fibroblast proliferation, and driving systemic acute-phase responses.
steps.say: Interleukin-1 is activated by the inflammasome to stimulate endothelial adhesion and systemic fever.

nodes.label: TLR Signaling Induces Synthesis of Cytosolic Precursor Pro-IL-1-Beta
Assembled NLRP3 Inflammasome Activates Caspase-1 to Cleave Pro-IL-1-Beta
Active 17-kDa IL-1-Beta Exocytosed Across Breached Plasma Membrane
Binds Type I IL-1 Receptors to Fire MyD88 and NF-Kappa-B Gene Targets

steps.tx: Both tumor necrosis factor and interleukin-one act as potent endogenous pyrogens that reset hypothalamic thermal regulation. Entering the preoptic hypothalamic circulation, they stimulate vascular endothelial cyclooxygenase-two to synthesize **prostaglandin E2**, which shifts the hypothalamic set point upward to induce fever, chills, and peripheral vasoconstriction.
steps.say: TNF and IL-1 stimulate hypothalamic COX-2 to produce PGE2, elevating the thermostat to induce fever.

left.title: Endogenous Pyrogen Cascade
points: TNF, IL-1-beta, and IL-6 circulate in bloodstream to brain vasculature
Interact with fenestrated capillaries of organum vasculosum (OVLT)
Induce endothelial cyclooxygenase-2 and microsomal PGE synthase-1
Prostaglandin E2 diffuses into preoptic nuclei, resetting set point to 39 C

right.title: Systemic Manifestations of Pyrexia
points: Cutaneous vasoconstriction reduces heat loss, producing subjective chills
Shivering thermogenesis increases metabolic heat production
Tachycardia: heart rate rises ~10 beats per minute per degree Celsius rise
Somnolence, malaise, and anorexia driven by central neuroinflammatory tone

steps.tx: While TNF and IL-one initiate early local vascular responses, interleukin-six functions as the chief systemic cytokine driving hepatic acute-phase protein production. Synthesized by macrophages and endothelial cells under IL-one stimulation, **interleukin-6 (IL-6)** stimulates hepatocytes to mass-produce C-reactive protein, serum amyloid A, and fibrinogen.
steps.say: Interleukin-6 acts on the liver to stimulate the mass synthesis of acute-phase proteins like CRP.

nodes.label: Activated Macrophages and Endothelial Cells Secrete Interleukin-6
Binds IL-6 Receptor Alpha and Signal-Transducing gp130 Homodimers
Activates Janus Kinase to Phosphorylate STAT3 Transcription Factor
Drives Massive Hepatic Transcription of CRP, SAA, Fibrinogen, and Hepcidin

steps.tx: In severe Gram-negative or Gram-positive bacteremia, massive lipopolysaccharide endotoxin loads trigger uncontrolled systemic release of TNF and IL-one into the bloodstream. This cytokine storm precipitates **septic shock**, characterized by severe systemic peripheral vasodilation, widespread microvascular permeability, hypotension, myocardial depression, and multiorgan failure.
steps.say: Uncontrolled systemic surges of TNF and IL-1 precipitate septic shock with severe hypotension and heart failure.

vis.caption: Massive systemic bacteremic vasodilation and multiorgan failure characteristic of septic shock.
vis.alt: Septic shock pathophysiology showing systemic vasodilation and multiorgan hypoperfusion

steps.tx: During severe septic shock, massive systemic TNF and IL-one levels downregulate endothelial thrombomodulin and protein C receptors while upregulating tissue factor expression. The resulting loss of the normal anticoagulant endothelial surface triggers disseminated intravascular coagulation, causing widespread **microvascular fibrin thrombi** that consume platelets and clotting factors.
steps.say: TNF and IL-1 downregulate thrombomodulin, triggering disseminated intravascular coagulation in sepsis.

nodes.label: Systemic Surges of TNF and IL-1 Damage Capillary Endothelial Linings
Downregulates Endothelial Anticoagulant Thrombomodulin and Protein C
Induces Endothelial and Monocyte Expression of Procoagulant Tissue Factor
Generates Widespread Microvascular Thrombi with Consumptive Coagulopathy

steps.tx: Within the pulmonary microcirculation, high concentrations of circulating TNF and interleukin-one damage alveolar capillary endothelial cells and fragile type one pneumocytes. Marked microvascular permeability produces severe non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, forming alveolar hyaline membranes characteristic of the life-threatening **acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)**.
steps.say: TNF-mediated alveolar capillary injury causes non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and ARDS.
